newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Jan-May budget gap at 53.8 pct of 1997 plan.
newsitem.headline: Polish Jan-May budget gap at 53.8 pct of 1997 plan.

text.p: Poland's budget deficit after the first five months of the year reached 53.8 percent of the 12.22 billion zloty shortfall planned for the whole of 1997, the government said on Tuesday.
It said in a statement budget revenues in the January-May period amounted to 35.3 percent of this year's plan while spending in the same period reached 37.1 percent.
The budget plan which assumes a deficit of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product envisages revenues of 115.33 billion zlotys and expenditures of 127.55 billion zlotys.
The statement did not give any amounts for spending, revenues and deficit for the January-May period and the finance ministry is due to release full preliminary results for the period next week.
At the end of April the budget deficit stood at 5.57 billion zlotys or 45.6 percent of the 1997 plan.
The statement said that in the same period of last year revenues reached 36.1 percent of the plan, spending 37.5 perdent and the deficit amounted to 51.9 percent of the plan.
